answer: A burn registry gates every new identity: an existing account destroys 5,000 POA publicly to anchor one, and the fee doubles for each extra identity that same account sponsors. The tokens are unrecoverable, so the registry records real spend, not names. A farmer minting 10,000 identities pays at least 50 million POA, and one sponsor anchoring ten sees the tenth burn alone cost 2.5 million. Each burn ripples outward as a visible tether no attacker can recover. The record is ferrous and append-only, so every jury sees what each sponsor paid.
